---
name: cis-agent-execution
description: Execute one approved CIS task through a discovered Codex or Claude provider with explicit modes, permissions, isolation, durable provenance, cancellation, resumption, and result reconciliation.
---

# CIS agent execution

1. Run `cis repo init --root <documentation-root>` when required. If initialization or command discovery fails, run `cis repo doctor` before retrying.
2. For pre-change BRD work, use `cis agent author brd` only with explicitly selected references. Then use `cis agent review brd` with a different provider, review mode, and read-only isolation; include extracted authoring evidence only after explicit disclosure authority. For delivery work, read `docs/references/agent-provider-profile.md`, the approved change plan, the selected ready task, and repository delivery policy.
3. Run `cis agent providers --format agent` and `cis agent provider diagnose <provider> --format agent`; provider availability never grants authority.
4. Run `cis agent prepare <change-id> <task-id> --provider <provider> --format agent` and inspect the bound digest and permission ceiling.
5. Run `cis agent run` with required provider, mode, permission and actor; select target and transport when needed. This command has no `--reason` option; retain rationale with the task. Workspace-write defaults to an isolated Git worktree whose baseline includes current tracked and non-ignored untracked changes.
6. Use `--approve-requests` only for explicitly authorized supported Codex requests within its declared ceiling. For Claude implementation tasks with workspace-write, optionally repeat `--allow-command` for reviewed literal commands. These native rules apply to one attempt, not read-only or document-authoring runs. They add permissions, not a shell/filesystem sandbox; native normalization, compound commands, directory changes and build-script effects remain relevant. A denied command is a failed attempt, not a waiting approval dialog.
7. Inspect durable state with `cis agent runs` and `cis agent show`; cancel with an actor and reason. Use `recover` only for a proven orphaned process before an explicit `resume`. A resumed attempt never erases the first attempt. Resume requires an explicit actor and reason. Supply any command list again; CIS restarts native session context when either attempt has a list. Retain actual tool outputs, not just the model's success claim.
8. Inspect the structured result before `cis agent import-result`. Imported output is evidence only; it cannot approve plans, accept designs, complete tasks, or verify delivery.

For direct plan/task runs under adopted engineering defaults (`requireTaskCompletion: true`), inspect `cis agent work status <change-id> --task <task-id>`. Resolve a missing allocation once through `cis agent work allocate <change-id> --input <allocation.json> --actor <authorized-controller> --reason <allocation-rationale>` using actual authorized task/change limits, reserve, decision and storage references, and an explicit acknowledgment of unmeasured historical effort. A provider profile, model output, new run ID, resume reason, or `--approve-requests` cannot grant or reset allocation. Missing or corrupt adopted accounting requires reconciliation. Product-document authoring and story execution remain outside this direct-task accounting slice; minimal import is unchanged.

Record one concise checkpoint through `cis agent work progress <change-id> <task-id> --input <checkpoint.json> --actor <controller>` at the first useful result and before broadening work. At the next safe admission boundary, cumulative active work reaching the adopted execution window (3,600 seconds in the reviewed profile, or an applicable narrower window) holds further expensive work until qualifying controller progress is recorded. Preserve Outcome / nonempty Evidence / measured Cost / Approach / Decision and the next bounded action; use current revisions and existing evidence. Automatic settlement or disposition summaries, status reads and model success claims do not qualify. Routine reflection may keep `closeAttempt: false` and continue the same logical attempt without another reviewer, human approval, or canonical task `Blocked` transition; all independent holds remain. Two logical attempts with the same blocker and no material new information hold unchanged expensive repetition; expected failing development tests do not count automatically. Use `cis agent work disposition` with a supported justified in-scope simplification or continuation under existing delegation, preserving spent work, hard limits, recovery uncertainty, and actual approval/permission gates.

Ordinary allocation redistribution cannot reduce protected task restoration reserves; repeat an existing reserve on update, because omitting it as zero is rejected when a nonzero reserve exists. For interrupted preparation, `work disposition reconcile` requires verified stopped ownership of the original preparing controller as well as its grace period. A live, other-host, unreadable or missing historical owner stays held; elapsed time and no provider PID alone prove nothing. Cancellation validates the bounded retained manifest/event/accounting evidence and can stop an independently verified live owned process despite uncertainty about another identity. Unverifiable processes remain untargeted; partial cleanup returns non-success and retains the reservation until every relevant owned identity is resolved and stopped. Preserve actor/reason, repository/run validation, evidence checks and recorded terminal provenance. Read the `cis agent work`, `cancel` and `recover` manuals for complete headless inputs and safe continuation.

For story work, inspect `cis brd feature wizard story status` and its delivery-size assessment, task contract and blocking reasons. Use explicit `assess`, `decompose` and `prepare --input` proposals as documented in the wizard-status manual; reading status never prepares work. Unknown/stale or above-medium delivery needs assessment or bounded child outcomes before implementation. A bounded sensitive task may still require high reasoning strength and independent review. Preserve instance IDs, work-owner links and exact prerequisites; use the resolved category, outputs, criteria and verification obligations for both implementation and review. Obtain `completion-context`, retain actual current evidence and use `complete` only when all applicable obligations and existing approval gates pass. Story implementation records retain their authority location; story review receipts use hash-verified participant copies of the retained read-only run as documented in story completion evidence. This carries task meaning; it does not extend direct-task accounting across the story correction loop.

Never copy provider credentials into CIS, infer permission from tool availability, run a non-ready task, bypass the design barrier for downstream work, or treat an agent's completion claim as canonical CIS state. Coordination, wireframe, and visual-design preparation establish the barrier and are therefore eligible before approval.

For command syntax, rule limits and current resumption behavior, read the `cis agent run` and `cis agent resume` manuals from the CIS distribution.
